tasks.short: Build the monthly HR reports for the board, HR Director and site managers from AFAS and Recruitee data.

today.trigger: Month close, a board meeting, or an ad hoc request from the HR Director or a site manager.
steps: Pull the AFAS extract and Recruitee pipeline export
Reconcile headcount, flex and verzuim figures in Excel
Refresh Power BI pages and copy charts into PowerPoint
Write the commentary per site
Mail the pack and answer follow-up questions
drudgery: Re-checking the same headcount reconciliation every month
today.time_sinks: Reconciling AFAS headcount against agency flex hours and rewriting commentary for three sites.

lenses.faster: Standard packs come from scheduled Power BI subscriptions with a drafted narrative; the analyst only checks numbers and edits the commentary, about 1 hour instead of a day per month.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh at month close triggers the pack; the narrative is drafted automatically and the analyst approves before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: A one-page weekly site pack for each of the three site managers and the night-shift leads, who get no tailored report today; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses pasting charts into PowerPoint; the analyst wants more time explaining why 90-day retention dropped at Venlo.
lenses.options: Little value in multiple drafts for standard packs; for board reports two framings of the same trend (site versus contract type) can change what the board asks for.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from producing packs to owning the KPI definitions and the narrative template; the analyst decides what goes in the standard pack and what stays ad hoc.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the HR cost lines of the monthly management report, after learning the AFAS general ledger structure

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which number will be misread at the board, and what is going on at a site that the data does not show.
tasks.pattern_why: Report content and refresh are fixed rules on an AFAS extract; only the commentary needs one model call, which sits inside the fixed workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh completes on the first working day after month close.
steps: Power BI refreshes the semantic model and runs data checks
Copilot in Power BI drafts a site-level summary of changes
Analyst checks outliers and edits the summary
Subscription mails the pack to the recipients
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves the narrative and any figure that moved more than a set threshold before the pack goes out.
data_needed: AFAS headcount, contracts and verzuim rates
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history and a SharePoint folder of sent packs with the approved narrative

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI summarises reports on a semantic model but can misinterpret data without a prepared model, and non-English chat is not officially supported.
Scheduled refresh and email subscriptions in Power BI handle distribution without a model.

risks: A wrong narrative is trusted because it reads well
research_questions: Does Noordhaven have Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity, and at what cost?
How often do the monthly figures need manual correction today?
Do site managers read the current pack, or only the headline?

tasks.short: Make sure the right managers get the right HR dashboards and figures on time, with the right access.

today.trigger: New manager, reorganisation, failed refresh or a complaint that numbers are late.
steps: Check nightly refresh status
Update row-level security and distribution lists
Chase AFAS or agency data that is late
Mail managers when a report is late or changed
drudgery: Updating access lists by hand after each org change
today.time_sinks: Keeping access in line with AFAS org changes and chasing agency hour files.

lenses.faster: Refresh monitoring, access sync from the AFAS org structure and late-data alerts run as scripts; the analyst handles only failures, saving most of the daily checking.
lenses.autonomous: An AFAS org-unit change triggers a proposed row-level security update; the analyst approves changes that widen access.
lenses.ambitious: Shift leads on night shifts get a short Teams digest of their team's absence and flex numbers, a group served for the first time; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses morning refresh checks; the analyst wants more time agreeing with managers what they actually need.
lenses.options: Not a decision task; one well-run process is enough.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the access model and the minimum group size rule, and decides who sees personal-level data.
reach: HR Administrator: maintaining manager-to-team mappings in AFAS, after learning the AFAS org structure screens

tasks.human_edge: Judging who should see personal data and handling the manager who insists on more access than the rules allow.
tasks.pattern_why: Refresh checks, access sync and alerts follow written rules; no model is needed.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly refresh finished or failed, or an AFAS org change is detected.
steps: Script checks refresh status and data completeness
Script compares AFAS manager hierarchy to Power BI security roles
Proposed access changes go to the analyst
Teams alert to managers if a report is late
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves any access change that adds personal-level data.
data_needed: AFAS org units and manager links
Power BI refresh and security role lists
in_practice.logs_to: Access change log on SharePoint, kept for audit and works council questions

evidence.claim: Power BI refresh failure alerts and row-level security can be scripted through its APIs.
Totals from a tool that holds per-user rows can still fall under works council consent.

risks: Access sync error exposes personal data (AVG breach)
Org data in AFAS is out of date
research_questions: How many access changes per month follow AFAS org changes?
Is the AFAS manager hierarchy reliable enough to drive security?
Has the works council agreed the current dashboard access rules?

tasks.short: Keep the AFAS extract, Power BI model and dashboards working and up to date as needs change.

today.trigger: Change request from HR, a new AFAS field, a CAO change or a broken measure.
steps: Read the change request and agree the definition
Change the extract or Power Query steps
Edit DAX measures and visuals
Test against known figures
Document and publish
drudgery: Hunting for which measure breaks after a field change
today.time_sinks: Debugging DAX and tracing where an AFAS field change broke the model.

lenses.faster: Copilot writes and explains DAX and documentation drafts, and a test suite of known figures flags breaks; the analyst still designs and reviews, saving about a third.
lenses.autonomous: Not suitable for autonomy; the analyst leads each change.
lenses.ambitious: A metric layer with written definitions for 90-day retention and verzuim that FP&A and HRBPs also query, a new service to Finance; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing documentation by hand; the analyst wants more time on definitions and model design.
lenses.options: Two or three DAX approaches for a tricky measure (e.g. 90-day retention with rehires) can change the result, so comparing them is worth it.
lenses.altitude: More expert: the analyst becomes owner of the semantic model and its tests, deciding definitions with the HR Director.
reach: FP&A Analyst: maintaining HR cost measures in the finance model, after learning the AFAS ledger extract

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the right definition (who counts as a hire, how flex workers count) and spotting a figure that is plausible but wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: Changes are different each time and the analyst must stay the lead on design and definitions.

in_practice.trigger: Change request logged by HR or a failing test after refresh.
steps: Analyst describes the change to Copilot
Copilot drafts DAX or Power Query and explains it
Test suite compares results to known figures
Analyst reviews, publishes and Copilot drafts the change note
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews every change before publishing.
in_practice.logs_to: Change log and model documentation on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX on Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity.

risks: Generated DAX that looks right but miscounts
Undocumented changes if the review step is skipped
research_questions: How many change requests a month, and how long does each take today?
Does Copilot-generated DAX pass the analyst's tests on Noordhaven's model?
Is there a test set of known figures to check against?

tasks.short: Answer managers' questions about dashboards and figures, and fix what they think is broken.

today.trigger: Teams message or mail from a manager or HRBP: 'this number looks wrong' or 'where do I find X'.
steps: Read the question and find the report
Check the figure against AFAS
Explain or fix the filter or measure
Reply to the manager
drudgery: Answering the same 'where do I find' questions
today.time_sinks: Repeat how-to questions and checking whether a figure is really wrong.

lenses.faster: A read-only assistant on the prepared model answers how-to and figure questions with verified answers; the analyst gets only misses and real defects.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's Teams question triggers the assistant; answers on group-level data go out directly, anything unclear or below the minimum group size goes to the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Shift leads and site managers in Tilburg and Venlo get answers at any hour, which today depend on the analyst's office hours; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses explaining the same filter; the analyst wants more time on questions that reveal a real data problem.
lenses.altitude: The analyst curates the verified answers and decides which questions the assistant may answer.
reach: HR Business Partner: first-line figure questions from managers, which the analyst can take over through the assistant

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a 'wrong number' is really a process problem at a site, and handling sensitive questions about individuals.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions cannot be predicted, so an agent queries the model, but misses and sensitive data go to the analyst.

in_practice.trigger: Manager asks a question in Teams or Power BI.
steps: Assistant states it is AI and checks the user's access
Answers from the prepared model or verified answers
Escalates unclear or small-group questions to the analyst
Analyst reviews misses weekly and adds verified answers
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst handles escalations and reviews a weekly sample of answers.
data_needed: Prepared semantic model with row-level security
in_practice.logs_to: Question and answer log reviewed weekly by the analyst

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers staffing data and warns faster access does not by itself lead to better decisions.
Chatbots must disclose they are AI under EU AI Act Art. 50.
Text-to-SQL cut query time from about 10 to 3 minutes at Uber, but hallucinated tables remain.

risks: Wrong answer trusted by a manager
research_questions: What share of questions to the analyst are repeat how-to questions?
How accurate is Copilot on Noordhaven's model with Dutch questions?
Does the works council need to consent to the assistant?

tasks.short: Track which managers and sites use HR dashboards and which have hiring or verzuim trouble, to target HR support.

today.trigger: Quarterly HR planning or an HRBP asking where to focus.
steps: Pull Power BI usage metrics
Compare sites on time to hire, 90-day retention and verzuim
Check agency fill rates per site
Summarise for HRBPs
drudgery: Combining three agency portal exports by hand
Building the same comparison table each quarter
today.time_sinks: Merging agency data with AFAS and Recruitee.

lenses.faster: A standing site-and-department watchlist built on the model flags units off-track and drafts a short note; the analyst checks and adds context.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly refresh triggers the watchlist; flagged departments are sent to the HRBP after the analyst checks them.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly agency scorecard (fill rate, 90-day stay of flex workers converted to hires) for the three staffing agencies, a new service to Procurement and the HR Director; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses merging agency exports; the analyst wants more time talking with HRBPs about why a site is off-track.
lenses.options: Different thresholds for flagging change which departments get attention, so showing two cut-offs is useful.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the flagging rules with the HR Director and decides which signals go to HRBPs.
reach: Recruiter: agency performance reporting, after learning agency contract terms

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the site story behind a red flag (a new manager, a peak season) before anyone acts on it.
tasks.pattern_why: Flags are threshold rules on known metrics; a model call only drafts the note.

steps: Script merges AFAS, Recruitee and agency data
Rules flag departments and agencies off-track (group level only)
Model drafts a short note per flag
Analyst checks and sends to HRBPs
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves every flag before it reaches an HRBP.
data_needed: Time to hire, 90-day retention and verzuim per department

evidence.claim: Dashboards able to observe performance usually need works council consent under WOR 27(1)(l).
Agency portals typically export orders and hours as files, so merging can be scripted.

risks: Department flags read as judgments on individual managers
Agency data formats change without notice
research_questions: Can the three agency portals export data in a stable format?
Do HRBPs act on the flags, or ignore them?
Does flagging departments need works council consent?

tasks.short: Build new dashboards, data models or Excel tools when HR needs something that does not exist yet.

today.trigger: New HR project, CAO change, new metric request or new data source.
steps: Agree requirements with the requester
Design the data model and extract
Build in Power BI or Excel
Test with the requester
Document and hand over
drudgery: Boilerplate Power Query and data cleaning code
today.time_sinks: Requirements back-and-forth and cleaning new data sources.

lenses.faster: AI coding tools draft the spec, cleaning scripts, DAX and documentation; the analyst designs and tests, cutting build time by about a third.
lenses.ambitious: A 'hire to productive' tracker joining Recruitee, AFAS and Studytube certificates (forklift, VCA) so site managers see when a new hire is cleared to work; a new service to site managers, and demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses boilerplate code; the analyst wants more time on design and data joins.
lenses.options: Two or three quick prototypes shown to the requester change what gets built, so drafting options is worth it.
lenses.altitude: More expert: the analyst builds more and faster, and decides which tools become part of the standard model.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: Studytube certificate expiry reporting, after learning Studytube's export

tasks.human_edge: Turning a vague request into the right question and judging which data is trustworthy.
tasks.pattern_why: Each build is different and needs the analyst's design decisions.

in_practice.trigger: Approved request for a new tool.
steps: Copilot drafts spec from the request
Analyst designs the model; AI drafts code and DAX
Analyst tests against known figures
AI drafts documentation; analyst publishes
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews and tests everything before release.
in_practice.logs_to: Project folder and change log on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX and can build report pages on a semantic model.

risks: Fast prototypes become unreviewed production tools
New personal data joins need a DPIA and works council review
research_questions: How many new builds a year, and how long do they take?
Can Studytube data be extracted automatically?
Would a new joined dataset need a DPIA under the AVG?

tasks.short: Keep HR records clean and compile figures on hires, leavers, transfers and verzuim for HR and the works council.

today.trigger: Monthly close, quarterly OR meeting, annual social report or a CBS/sector survey.
steps: Check AFAS records for errors (missing end dates, open sick reports)
Ask HR administrators to correct them
Compile counts and verzuim rates
Format the tables for the requester
drudgery: Finding the same data errors every month
today.time_sinks: Chasing data corrections before figures can be trusted.

lenses.faster: Data checks run nightly and route errors to HR administrators with a plain explanation; standard counts and verzuim rates come from the model, saving most of the compiling.
lenses.autonomous: Nightly refresh triggers checks; the HR administrator corrects in AFAS; required filings get analyst approval.
lenses.ambitious: 90-day retention and verzuim correct by day 2 of each month instead of week 2, so the HR Director decides on the North Star monthly with reliable figures; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting for missing end dates; the analyst wants more time on what the figures mean.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the data quality rules and decides which errors block a report.
reach: HR Administrator: monthly data quality checks, which the analyst takes over through rules

tasks.human_edge: Deciding how to count edge cases (rehires, flex conversions, long-term sick) and keeping causes of sick leave out of the data.
tasks.pattern_why: Checks and counts are fixed rules; a model call only writes the error explanation.

steps: Rules check missing end dates, open sick reports, mismatched contracts
Model writes a plain explanation per error
Errors go to HR administrators as a task list
Counts and verzuim rates refresh in Power BI
in_practice.human_gate: HR administrator corrects in AFAS; analyst approves figures for OR and external filings.
data_needed: AFAS employee, contract and absence records (dates and durations only)
in_practice.logs_to: Data quality log with open and closed errors

evidence.claim: Absence data is health data under GDPR Art. 9.
The Dutch DPA fined a firm €15,000 partly for recording the cause of sick leave.

risks: Sick-leave causes slip into free-text fields
research_questions: Which AFAS errors recur most and how many per month?
How long after month end are figures reliable today?
Do HR administrators have time to act on daily error lists?

tasks.short: Follow labour market, wage and sector trends in Dutch logistics and explain what they mean for our hiring and pay.

today.trigger: CAO negotiations, annual workforce planning, or the HR Director asking about a trend.
steps: Read CBS, UWV, sector and agency reports
Pull relevant figures into Excel
Compare with Noordhaven data per site
Write a short memo
drudgery: Reading long reports for one relevant figure
today.time_sinks: Finding and reading sources, then aligning them with internal data.

lenses.faster: A model summarises new sources with citations and caveats and places them next to internal figures; the analyst checks sources and writes the conclusion.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly scan drafts a trend brief with sources; the analyst approves before it goes to the HR Director.
lenses.ambitious: A quarterly site labour-market brief for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo for the HR Director and Recruiters, used in vacancy and flex planning; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses skimming long reports; the analyst wants more time on what a trend means for Venlo's night shift hiring.
lenses.options: Scenarios (e.g. tight vs. easing labour market) change flex and hiring plans, so drafting two or three is worth it.
lenses.altitude: The analyst becomes the HR Director's advisor on workforce scenarios, owning the assumptions.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: market pay benchmark summaries, after learning CAO pay scales
FP&A Analyst: headcount assumptions for the budget

tasks.human_edge: Judging which source is reliable and how a trend applies to Noordhaven; keeping caveats about causation.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns long sources into a checkable summary with citations inside a fixed monthly routine.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule or a request from the HR Director.
steps: Fetch new releases from listed sources
Model summarises each with citation and caveats
Model places them next to internal site figures
Analyst checks and writes the conclusion
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst checks every cited figure before the brief is shared.
data_needed: Internal hiring, retention and pay figures
in_practice.logs_to: Trend brief archive on SharePoint with source links

evidence.claim: Trend reports often cannot attribute cause; Workday's own data 'does not establish how much of the decline AI caused'.
Self-reported survey data runs high: 48% of employees exaggerated their AI use.

risks: Wrong or invented figures in summaries
research_questions: Which sources does the HR Director trust and use today?
Has a trend memo ever changed a hiring or CAO decision?
How accurate are model summaries of Dutch CBS/UWV reports?

role.altitude: From producing reports to owning HR's metric layer: the definitions, verified answers, access rules and data checks that managers and assistants query, plus advising the HR Director on workforce scenarios.
reach: FP&A Analyst: HR cost lines and headcount assumptions in the budget
HR Administrator: monthly AFAS data quality checks
HR Business Partner: first-line figure questions from managers
Learning and Development Specialist: certificate expiry reporting from Studytube
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality in AFAS and agency portals, Power BI capacity for Copilot, works council consent for anything that can observe performance, and AVG rules on health data; perhaps 40-45% of current hours freed, but interpretation and definitions stay human.
skills_to_grow: Writing verified answers and access rules for AI assistants
AVG/GDPR and WOR consent basics for analytics
Explaining figures to the board and works council
role.ambitious_version: Run a hire-to-productive service that tells each site manager weekly which roles are open, which new hires are cleared to work, and which teams risk losing people before day 90, at group level and with works council consent.
